newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia beats Oct tax targets as arrears flow in.
newsitem.headline: Russia beats Oct tax targets as arrears flow in.

text.p: Russia slightly exceeded its tax revenue targets in October as debtors paid up, but officials said on Wednesday they would launch bankruptcy proceedings against two new debtors and warned other companies to pay.

Pyotr Mostovoi, head of the Federal Bankruptcy Agency, told a news conference that October tax revenues were 101 percent of planned levels after some companies paid tax arrears. September revenues were just 48 percent of target.

Low tax revenues are one of Russia's most pressing economic problems and the International Monetary Fund last month delayed payment of the next tranche of a $10 billion three-year loan because it was worried about this.
A group of IMF tax specialists is looking at this month's figures and Finance Minister Alexander Livshits said on Monday that the talks were difficult.
The government, admitting that raking in extra tax debts was essential, has set up a special emergency commission to force indebted companies to pay.

A statement distributed at Mostovoi's news conference said that higher October revenues showed that the commission, dubbed the VChK, had been responsible for a shift in attitudes in boardrooms across Russia.
"This shows brilliantly that, with the creation of the VChK, there has been a shift in the attitude of many company managers towards their duty to pay taxes," the statement said.
The threat of bankruptcy is one of the commission's main weapons, but government officials have also said that managers could be held personally responsible if their firms did not pay their bills.
Bankruptcy proceedings have been started against six firms including Moscow's Moskvich carmaker and the Krasnodarnefteorgsintez oil refinery, which is part of state-owned Rosneft.
Mostovoi said the government would now file bankruptcy proceedings against the Korshunovsky ore enriching factory and Tashtagolskoye mining management firm.

Mostovoi said the government had notified 16 other companies, including AO Norilskgazprom, part of RAO Norilsk Nickel and AO Tebukneft, one of KomiTEK oil group production units, that they must pay overdue taxes within a week.
He said management at these firms must report to the government about their financial status and if it is clear they cannot pay the government will start bankruptcy proceedings.
He said about 35 companies paid less than 20 percent of current taxes.
